mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate activity (HOUST) over two months signals a strengthening demand side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the proxy shows sustained increase.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as production cuts and inventory adjustments impact corporate earnings.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% month-over-month and CPIAUCSL increases by less than 0.1% in the same period, it signals strong real demand growth without significant inflationary pressure, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases < 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% year-over-year, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% over three months signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as wage pressures and consumer spending increase.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where the proxy shows sustained decline.
